column1: # Game profile of Kirby Star Allies (Switch, update 4.0.0a = v393216)
# PEANUTS: a Peanuts Native profile (Banana Native has none for this title); whole file Peanuts' own
# HAL Laboratory's own engine on NintendoWare (G3d, Font, Ui2d, Vfx, Atk), SDK 4.4.1, NVN; subsdk0 is the movie module (MP4 cinematics).
# The shaders are BNSH archives inside HAL's .cmp containers under gfx/, ptcl/ and lyt/, in the loose shader/ files and embedded in main (shader_split.py).
# Status: plays (README.md); the memory rows are the survey's guess (dm/games/profile_guess.py), the peaks measured in play are in the note
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon (Big Brain Academy: Brain vs. Brain sets a heap only then)
# PEANUTS: the game paces itself in whole vsyncs: an interval index at [main+0x54c5b0]+0 picks the vsyncs a frame from the table at main+0x3b5ac8 (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
# so 60, 30, 20 (and 15, not offered) fps; no index gives half a vsync, so nothing above 60. Reviewed from the FPSLocker Warehouse config for this build (01007E3006DDA000/D55608916FA56C18.yaml,
# v4; interval offsets found by Kirby567Fan): the index is 60 / fps - 1 (vsync_index_u32), and the game's own setter (main+0x5a4c, str w1, [x0]) is a NOP so it cannot put
# it back. The config's "remove double buffer" writes are not taken: the host presents the game's frames itself. Game owned (the default) is the game's own 60
# PEANUTS: the default cap is 60, measured on Turnip 27.0.0-R2 (README.md, Status); 30 and 20 are experimental (Open)
